title: devbin test all run from a terminal hangs forever at the read-only replace_file arm, because rename_staged's mv prompts when stdin is a tty
body:
**`bin/devbin test all` run from a terminal stops dead at the read-only `replace_file` arm and never returns, because `rename_staged` calls `mv` without `-f` and POSIX `mv` prompts when the destination exists, permissions do not allow writing it, and stdin is a tty.**

## Measured

hv ran `dvb test all` at 21:26Z on 2026-09-17 from an interactive terminal. The log printed `ok 652` at 21:35Z and then nothing. hv interrupted it at 05:48Z: **quiet for 8h13m, 8h22m elapsed**, exit 141, `tee failed writing ... the log is untrustworthy for this run`.

- Last line of `tmp/test/20260917-2126.bats.out`: `ok 652 stage_beside gives a file that does not exist yet the mode the umask gives a new file, under any umask`.
- Test 653 is `tests/unit/helpers.bats:857`, "replace_file replaces a read-only file, and it stays read-only". It `chmod 444`s the target and calls `replace_file`.
- `replace_file` -> `stage_beside` -> `rename_staged` (lib/helpers:536), which called `mv "$1" "$file"`.
- The prompt, driven here under a pty, verbatim: `override r--r--r--  matts/staff for /.../f? (y/n [n])`.
- With stdin not a tty: rc 0, silent, no prompt at all.
- With `mv -f` under a pty: no prompt, and the target keeps its mode `-r--r--r--`, which is what the test asserts.
- Census: the runtime has exactly **two** `mv` calls. `lib/install:379` already wrote `mv -f`. `lib/helpers:538` had not.

## Why it survived every run that has ever been made of this suite

**The prompt is tty-gated, and nothing that normally runs the suite has a tty.** Every agent run, and both CI jobs, have stdin redirected, so `mv` never asks and the arm passes. The one class of runner it hangs for is a human at a terminal -- who is also the only one who cannot see a TAP line explaining it, because there is no output at all.

**So this is a false green that is green for everyone able to observe it**, and the suite that contains the hanging test is the same suite that reported 1372 ok at `e3f1231`. Nothing was wrong with that count; the run simply could not reach the condition.

## Reach beyond the suite

`replace_file` and `sed_inplace` are how devbin rewrites files it does not own the mode of -- the version stamp, the fleet doc fold (0084), the notes renderers. **Any devbin command that replaces a read-only file, run from a terminal, blocks the same way.** The test is where it was found, not the limit of it.

## Fixed

`rename_staged` uses `mv -f`, matching `lib/install:379`.

**Arm**: `tests/unit/helpers.bats`, "every mv in the RUNTIME carries -f, so no replace can stop on a terminal prompt". Driven red first against the un-fixed line, failing at its own assertion and naming `lib/helpers:549`.

**The arm is lexical and that is a declared limit, not an oversight.** The behaviour is tty-gated and a bats run has no tty, so no arm in this suite can watch the prompt appear. What it holds is that no `mv` in the runtime is left able to ask. **That sentence originally said the arm "cannot tell `-f` from `-if`", and it was wrong in the reassuring direction** -- see Review below: `-if` is safe, and the forms the regex actually lets through are `-fi`, `-f -i` and `-fn`. A prompt reached by any other command is outside it. **Tests are excluded deliberately**: nineteen bare `mv` calls live under `tests/`, each moving a file the test just created and can write, so none can prompt today -- but a test that moved over a read-only fixture would hang the suite identically and this arm would not see it.

## The class this belongs to, not yet censused

Any external command devbin runs that can block on a terminal: a prompt, a pager, an editor, a credential or host-key ask. `git` paging when stdout is a tty is the first candidate and has not been checked. That census is assigned and is not part of this issue.

## Note for the sweep

`lib/helpers` is vendored, so this change goes in the next fleet sweep's pre-notice.

## Review (dc, 2026-09-18) and the first terminal run

**The block is REPRODUCED, not inferred.** vc could not stage it under `script`, which hands mv an immediate EOF. dc drove it with python3 `pty.fork()`, read-only destination, 2s budget:

| form       | result  | dst |
| ---------- | ------- | --- |
| `mv`       | BLOCKED | old |
| `mv -f`    | exits   | new |
| `mv -if`   | exits   | new |
| `mv -fi`   | BLOCKED | old |
| `mv -i -f` | exits   | new |
| `mv -f -i` | BLOCKED | old |
| `mv -n`    | exits   | old |
| `mv -fn`   | exits   | old |

On BSD mv the LAST of -f/-i/-n wins. **The arm's regex accepts `-fi` and `-f -i`, which block, and `-fn`, which exits 0 WITHOUT replacing the file while rename_staged reports success -- a silent error, worse than the hang.** The declared limit named `-if`, which is safe, so it pointed away from the real holes.

The `tests/` census of 19 bare `mv` calls is confirmed; none shares a test with a write-removing chmod.

**First behavioural evidence of the fix:** hv's `dvb test all` from a terminal at `3fcc71a`, 2026-09-18 06:01Z-06:17Z, 1377 ok, 0 not ok (`tmp/test/20260918-0601.bats.*`); the read-only arm, now test 654, passed where the previous run stopped for 8h13m.

**Before close:** (a) the arm accepts only `mv -f` with no later -i/-n and is driven red against `-fi`, `-f -i`, `-fn` and bare `mv`; (b) the arm's own stated limit reworded to match. A behavioural pty arm is built once inside the terminal-blocking census (hv, 2026-09-18) and must fail loudly, not skip, where a pty should have been available.

## Closed

**What holds it now is an exact allowlist, not a rule about flags** (dc, round three, `2457113`). Two lexical rounds (`9abd0ba`, `c910104`) were each beaten by spellings they did not read: a second `mv` after `;` or `&&`, an `-i` on a continuation line, a quoted `'-n'`. The arm now holds that the runtime's lines naming `mv` are exactly `lib/helpers`'s `if ! mv -f "$1" "$file"; then` and `lib/install`'s `mv -f "$tmp" "$dst" || {`, byte for byte. Any other line naming `mv` in `lib/` or `bin/` is a finding, and a known line that disappears fails too. Routing `lib/install` through `rename_staged`, which would have left one `mv`, was measured and refused: a mktemp stage is 0600 and `cp` keeps it, so every vendored file would land 0600.

**vc's mutants against round three** (scratch worktree, `scratchpad/mut-0086d.py`): the known line duplicated in its own file, a bare `mv` in a hidden directory (`lib/cmd/.lib`), a trailing comment on the known line, `-i` on a continuation of the install line, a `mv()` shadow calling `/bin/mv -i`, and a tab-indented bare `mv` each die. **Two live, and are declared rather than closed**: `mv` spelled so its text does not read `mv` -- `"m""v"` or `m\v` -- added beside the known lines. Nobody writes those by accident; the arm's limit now names them beside variables, aliases and functions of another name.

**Behavioural evidence**: hv's terminal run at `3fcc71a`, 1377/0. The behavioural arm is 0088's, on `run_tty_eof`, where bare `mv` exits 0 without replacing and `mv -f` replaces.
